references.observation: The inspected public hero table exposes seasons, mode switches, matches and per-minute statistics rather than a single overall strength score.
references.principle: Keep quantitative context and sample size next to every conclusion.
references.application: Retain separated ranked and quick-play selectors and label the season on each plotted result.
references.avoid: Do not copy external branding or portray a public table as a certified measurement of hidden tactical impact.

references.observation: The second profile has a distinct hero pool, so switching accounts must visibly change the evidence and mechanical interpretation.
references.principle: A shared reading shell can retain separate player identity and evidence.
references.application: Use a persistent account selector and retain the same chapter during switches.
references.avoid: Do not copy external branding or portray a public table as a certified measurement of hidden tactical impact.

references.observation: The existing user-reviewed report uses cream paper, dark chapter navigation, lime evidence highlights and selectable hero analysis.
references.principle: Port the approved information hierarchy and visual language without introducing a new decorative theme.
references.application: Keep the original ten chapters, dossier block, evidence tables and seasonal dot chart in the standalone app.
references.avoid: Do not copy external branding or portray a public table as a certified measurement of hidden tactical impact.

concepts.medium: DOM reading document with inline SVG evidence plots.
concepts.composition: Chapter rail and full-height scrollable editorial dossier.
concepts.interaction: Account switching and contextual seasonal table filtering.
concepts.motion: Immediate data replacement with optional smooth chapter scrolling.
concepts.rationale: Selected because this is an existing approved analytical report with dense text and real table inspection.

concepts.medium: Canvas chronological map of a career with zoomable match nodes.
concepts.composition: An uninterrupted horizontal career field with floating detail lenses.
concepts.interaction: Pinch and drag through seasons before opening individual nodes.
concepts.motion: Spatial pan inertia and animated semantic zoom between seasons.
concepts.rationale: Rejected because map-first exploration makes long explanations and precise sample boundaries harder to read on phones.

concepts.medium: Paged SVG poster deck of hero scouting illustrations.
concepts.composition: One hero fills a portrait page with a minimal bottom index.
concepts.interaction: Swipe between individual hero posters and flip to evidence.
concepts.motion: Directional page folding and card flipping between summaries.
concepts.rationale: Rejected because hiding evidence on card backs slows the explicit comparison of season and mode context.

selection.reason: Preserve the report the user already reviewed while making the whole analysis independently installable and readable offline.

assets.role: Original installation mark for the personal scouting notebook.
assets.acceptance: Recognizable R-and-slash silhouette at small home-screen icon sizes, no generated Forge monogram.

risks: Dense numeric tables must scroll internally without expanding the phone viewport.
Optional remote portraits can disappear offline without hiding evidence or controls.
comparisons: Desktop first frame versus phone first frame of the same report.
Hero progression with data versus a genuinely empty search or seasonal slice.
